title: kv-cache: improve memory management and eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation and spillover
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: We continue to observe KV cache fragmentation and frequent spillover under mixed-length workloads which increases GPU memory pressure and triggers expensive paging. This PR implements a set of memory-management and eviction heuristic changes to reduce fragmentation, improve spillover behavior, and prioritize hot KV shards for defragmentation. Summary of changes: 1) compacting allocator for pinned KV pages: introduces a background compaction pass that coalesces free regions for long-lived pinned allocations to reduce fragmentation. 2) spillover-aware eviction priority: eviction now scores entries by combined recency, size, and spill likelihood; large cold blobs that cause immediate spillover are deprioritized for eviction in favor of smaller high-cost entries. 3) multi-tier paging thresholds: dynamic thresholds per-shard that increase tolerance for temporary memory pressure and trigger spillover only when useful; this reduces oscillation between spill and rehydrate cycles. 4) defrag scheduling improvements: defragmentation now runs as cooperative low-priority work on idle CPU/GPU cycles and is throttled by observed request latency to avoid SLO regressions. 5) telemetry and tracing: adds new metrics for fragmentation ratio, compaction time, spill events per-minute and per-shard leak counters, plus dashboard panels and alert rules recommended in the PR description. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests for allocator and scoring - [x] integration test with mixed-length workload harness - [x] perf microbenchmarks and long-run soak tests - [x] documentation updates for config knobs Related: ENG-9384 describes production incidents where multiple small requests caused a cascading spill. ENG-9472 is the follow-up to the initial spillover mitigation work. Production impact: In long-run soak tests with representative customer traces we see median GPU memory headroom increase by ~23% (less fragmentation), 62% reduction in spill events, and tail request latency P99 increase of <=1.5ms in the worst-case stress tests. Backwards compatibility: config knobs default to current safe values so no operator changes required. Testing: included unit tests, integration harness runs in CI, and an additional canary on redwood/perf-canary for 48h soak with no regression signals. Implementation notes: most changes are localized to runtime/kv_cache and runtime/scheduler with a small runtime/config surface to expose per-shard thresholds. See files_changed for details.

review_comments: Jordan Lee: Nice consolidation. Two concerns: 1) the compaction worker locking needs to avoid holding allocator-level locks across GPU memcpy operations, can you refactor to use a handoff buffer? 2) please add a telemetry tag for shard_id on spill events so we can correlate with tenant traffic.
Asha Patel: Addressed both. Compaction now uses a handoff buffer and memmove is performed outside the allocator lock. Added shard_id label to spill metrics. See commit b4d2e5f and d2a8c33.
Miguel Torres: Eviction scoring looks good, but I'd like to see a small sensitivity test for scoring weights. Can we add a short unit test that fuzzes weights and validates spill reduction trends?
Asha Patel: Added scoring sensitivity test and fixed an edge-case where very large KV entries could starve younger entries. See commit c7e9f10.
Priya Nair: Runbook and config docs look thorough. One nit: clarify default value units (MB vs MiB).
Asha Patel: Clarified units in docs and in yaml comments.
